description: Starting from the equal-third throughput, Jain fairness and service reward, increase one component to 0.50 at a time and reduce the other two equally to 0.25. This round measures the direction and strength of each component before any local tuning.

common.reward_normalization: Use the existing bounded throughput, Jain fairness and service scores. The equal-third case is the center reference. In each new case, one coefficient is raised to 0.50 and the other two are reduced equally to 0.25. All undeclared rewards, standalone penalties, reward deltas and Lagrangian multipliers remain disabled.

cases.label: Throughput-heavy: 50% throughput, 25% Jain, 25% service
cases.hypothesis: When throughput is increased while Jain and service are reduced equally, does goodput improve, and how much fairness, UE coverage and waiting time are lost?

cases.label: Jain-heavy: 25% throughput, 50% Jain, 25% service
cases.hypothesis: When Jain fairness is increased while throughput and service are reduced equally, does deterministic fairness and UE rotation improve without causing a flat-priority collapse?

cases.label: Service-heavy: 25% throughput, 25% Jain, 50% service
cases.hypothesis: When service is increased while throughput and Jain are reduced equally, does waiting time improve enough to justify the cost in goodput and fairness?
